body_markdown:
We certainly had fun with this one, mostly because we all love the James Bond franchise. There’s a new Bond in town,[Robert Pattinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Pattinson) , and we think he needs a new ride before he hits the silver screen. There will probably never be a vehicular choice better than the[Aston Martin DB5](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/neglected-aston-martin-db5-finally-gets-the-restoration-it-deserves/) , and there might not be a better 007 than Sean Connery. Conversely, there was some controversy when Pierce Brosnan drove the brand new BMW Z3 in *GoldenEye* (1995), but we aren’t necessarily looking at the past.


The new Bond opens new doors for his vehicle, and the time is now to think about what that vehicle should be. So let’s get into a conversation with the staff here at Hagerty Media, and please chime in with your thoughts in the comments below!


## Aston Martin


Victor


Aston Martin/Max Earey


Cygnet


Aston Martin


V8 Vantage


[Nik Berg](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/nberg/)


“If it’s still an Aston, it has gotta be the Victor.” — *Isaac Shapiro*


“I don’t think the Cygnet has been used yet.” — *Adam Wilcox*


“As expensive as restomods are, and as popular as the ’80s have become, I think a subtly restomodded V8 Vantage in a traditional lighter shade of green would usher in the Pattinson era well.” — *Eddy Eckart*


## Bentley


Bentley


Bentley


“Any reader of Ian Fleming’s books would have to agree that James Bond is a Bentley man. The original books had him driving a blower Bentley, so it would be fitting that James Bond should drive a kitted out Continental GT.” — *Greg Ingold*


“An older Continental R would be pretty sweet.” — *Adam Wilcox*


## Rimac


Rimac


“I think the Pattinson Bond needs to be driving an electric supercar like the Rimac Nevera R.” — *Joe DeMatio*


## Morgan


Morgan


“He’s British, he’s haute couture, he’s got a handle on tech when he needs to, but he’s ultimately a throwback from an older era. A dinosaur in the latest threads, so he needs to drive a Morgan Supersport 400.” — *Eric Weiner*


## Lotus


Lotus Emira


[Cameron Neveu](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/cameron-neveu/)


Lotus Evija


Lotus


“A new Lotus. Not sure what new Lotus might fit, but Pattinson seems to be a little different than the last few Bonds, but not too much of a departure. Maybe returning Bond to the driver’s seat of a Lotus would get a fresh car on screen while keeping half true to the timeline.” — *Kyle Smith*


“I love the Lotus idea that Kyle suggested. Joe’s also got a point with the electric supercar pick, so my money is on the current Lotus electric supercar, the Evija. Do I like that option? *Kiiiinda* . A vintage Esprit would be way, way cooler—and vintage is cool now, so it would be very fitting.” — *Grace Jarvis*


## Jaguar


Jaguar


“In keeping with the British theme, I think he’ll drive that Jaguar Type 01. I think they’re going to put him in an electric vehicle for virtue signaling, and that quite annoys me. The whole point of the James Bond thing is that he defies the march of time ( *hello to Dame Judi Dench’s wonderful testimony scene in Skyfall* ), but I have a feeling that outside pressure will be too much and he won’t drive something that burns dino juice.” — *Nathan Petroelje*


“I hate to admit it, but I like this better than the BMW Z3 from *Goldeneye* . Bond in a four-banger German roadster will likely always be 007’s low point for me.” — *Sajeev Mehta*


## Sajeev And His Curveballs


Tesla


Slate Automotive


“Hold up, don’t consider my choices as rage bait! Well, at least not yet: Apparently, the act of picking Robert Pattinson also involved the input of a man named Jeff Bezos. *Yeah, that Bezos* .


He was quoted as being ‘heavily involved’ in the selection process, and that knowledge skewed my opinion on this matter. Considering how everything is now tech-forward, I initially thought the gadgety design (four-wheel steering, crazy steering wheel, etc.) and austere styling of the Tesla Cybertruck would work for a spy that cavorts in elite social circles. It’s not legal in the EU or the U.K., but it wouldn’t be out of place if the movie was set in America.


But the Cybertruck is officially dead, so no marketing dollars can be funneled from Tesla to MGM studios. So instead I leaned harder into the Bezos connection. It’s clear that the new Amazon/MGM star of this famous franchise needs to be in a[Slate EV truck](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/picture-car-confidential/picture-car-confidential-45-slate-first-drive/#:~:text=he%20persuaded%20his%20old%20boss%20Jeff%20Bezos%20to%20invest%20%24100%20million%20in%20Slate.) .” — *Sajeev Mehta*
